ExpertSleepers-Encoders-8CV.notes: Source read at commit 95496e8 ("Version 2.1.0. Added Categories."), the HEAD of https://github.com/expertsleepersltd/vcvrack-encoders; its plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed 2.1.0 manifest. Each input is sampled once per eight process calls rather than every sample: 8CV.cpp:18-19 derive a phase state and a DAC index, and line 25 reads inputs[dac] only when the state is 0. The panel prints the inputs 1 to 8, which are indices 0 to 7. The clip limits are -2048 and 2047 counts, so the positive limit is fractionally lower than the negative one; both are quoted as about 5.33V. The local smuxProof at 8CV.cpp:30 is hardcoded false, so the phase increment is always 2 and the alternative branch can never run. No family is given for the output because it carries a coded word rather than a signal of any of the four kinds.

ExpertSleepers-Encoders-8GT.notes: Source read at commit 95496e8, HEAD of the maker's repository; its plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed 2.1.0 manifest. The bit test is a hysteresis pair written out by hand rather than a SchmittTrigger, with the same 1.0f and 0.5f thresholds. The output voltage is literally the eight-bit pattern as a number, so it runs from 0V to 255V; no family is given because it is a coded word rather than a signal of any of the four kinds. The panel prints the inputs 1 to 8, which are indices 0 to 7.

ExpertSleepers-Encoders-ES5.notes: Source read at commit 95496e8, HEAD of the maker's repository; its plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed 2.1.0 manifest. Inputs 0, 1, 2 become the high, middle and low bytes of the left word and inputs 3, 4, 5 the same three bytes of the right word (ES5.cpp:45-46), which is why the outputs are described as carrying the first three and the last three. The Category menu (ES5.cpp:98-118) is a submenu named Category holding A, B and C; it selects the divisor at lines 49 to 63 — 0x800000 for A, 0x7fff80 for B and 0x7fffff for C. The maker's page at expert-sleepers.co.uk/vcvrack_encoders.html does not mention it, and the commit that added it is titled only "Added Categories", so no purpose is claimed for it here. The outputs are given no family: they carry encoded words destined for a DAC rather than audio, control voltage, pitch or a trigger. The panel prints the inputs 1 to 6 and leaves the outputs unlabelled; left and right come from the source.

ExpertSleepers-Encoders-ES40.notes: Source read at commit 95496e8, HEAD of the maker's repository; its plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed 2.1.0 manifest. ES40.cpp:45-46 pack inputs 0 and 1 into the high and middle bytes of the left word and inputs 2 and 3 into the same bytes of the right, then split input 4: (b[4] << 0) & 0xf0 goes into the low byte of the left word and (b[4] << 4) & 0xf0 into the low byte of the right, so the fifth header is the only one that does not get a whole byte and the low four bits of each word are always zero. The Category menu is the same submenu as on the ES-5 Encoder, selecting 0x800000, 0x7fff80 or 0x7fffff; the maker's page does not mention it. The outputs are given no family: they carry encoded words destined for a DAC rather than audio, control voltage, pitch or a trigger. The panel prints the inputs 1 to 5 and leaves the outputs unlabelled; left and right come from the source.

lines: Corrects the voltage scaling of a DC-coupled audio interface that has no calibration of its own, so that a volt in Rack is a volt in the eurorack system
Note — Calibration needs a 3V reference from your eurorack system, and a cable from the audio interface's physical output back to its own input.
Note — Press Calibrate Input, carry out the step named in the panel display, then press the button again to confirm it; repeat until the display reads Idle, then do the same with Calibrate Output.
Note — Before either calibration has been run the module passes both signals through unchanged, and the two calibrations are stored with the patch.
Note — The panel display is a text window rather than a control, so it cannot be clicked for help; it names the step to carry out and reads Idle when nothing is in progress.
Starts the input calibration and confirms each of its steps; the lamp flashes between presses and the display names what to do
Starts the output calibration and confirms its first step; the module then drives its own To Device jack to 0V and to 3V and measures each of them through From Device
The signal coming back from the audio interface, rescaled by the measured input calibration before it reaches To VCV; every calibration measurement is taken from this jack
The signal from the interface with the input calibration applied, so that a volt read here is a volt at the interface
The signal to be sent out to the interface; it is pre-compensated by the measured output calibration before it reaches To Device
The pre-compensated signal for the audio interface output; during output calibration the module drives this jack itself, to 0V and then to 3V

ExpertSleepers-Encoders-Calibrator.notes: Source read at commit 95496e8, HEAD of the maker's repository; its plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed 2.1.0 manifest. Each calibration point is the median of 20000 samples (kNumSamples, Calibrator.cpp:6 and 240-244), and the output calibration allows half a second of settling between driving 3V and measuring it (line 205). The defaults are in0V 0, in3V 3, out0V 0, out3V 3, which make both corrections the identity — hence the note that an uncalibrated module passes signals through. Initialise resets those four values (onReset, lines 52-58) but leaves the state machine where it is. The two lamps are driven from the button parameters themselves except while a confirmation is outstanding, when they are toggled at ten times a second. No family is given for any of the four jacks: what they carry is whatever is being calibrated. The panel prints From Device, To VCV, From VCV and To Device beside the jacks, and Calibrate Input and Calibrate Output beside the buttons.

lines: Packs four signals into a stereo pair, alternating two of them on each output sample by sample, for an ES-3 fed over ADAT
Note — The outputs go to a stereo pair of audio channels driving an ES-3, and the interface has to run at 88.2kHz or 96kHz for the hardware to separate the pairs again.
Note — Each output alternates between two inputs on successive samples, so what comes out of it is not a signal that can be listened to or patched anywhere else in Rack.

Swaps the order of the two signals packed onto the R output; the lamp is lit while they are swapped, and the setting is stored with the patch
The left half of the multiplexed pair, alternating between the first two inputs; patch it to one channel of the stereo pair driving the ES-3
The right half of the multiplexed pair, alternating between the last two inputs; patch it to the other channel of that pair

ExpertSleepers-Encoders-SMUX.notes: Source read at commit 95496e8, HEAD of the maker's repository; its plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed 2.1.0 manifest. All four inputs are read only on the even half of the parity (SMUX.cpp:70-76), so each is effectively sampled at half the engine rate; the two outputs then replay the stored pair one value per sample. Flip is implemented as an index offset — inputs[m_flipL] and inputs[1-m_flipL] — so it exchanges which of the two left inputs is written into the first slot, and the same for the right. The buttons are momentary LEDButtons feeding SchmittTriggers, so each press toggles the stored flip rather than holding it. No family is given for any jack: the inputs carry whatever is sent to the hardware and the outputs carry an interleaved stream. The panel prints the inputs 1 to 4, the buttons Flip L and Flip R, and the outputs L and R.
